absent: Selection rule between the two fault lookup variants and their callers is not shown.
Detailed guard upgrade, downgrade, and careful acquisition semantics beyond success and failure outcomes.
Stack growth behavior when memory management is present.
Capacity and layout of the table batch and gather structures and flush thresholds.
Full callback sets for interval and classic notifiers and their blocking constraints.
Implementations of sleepable RCU, spin, nested write lock, list, lockless list, interval tree, and warning helpers.
Lifetime, allocation failure handling beyond local cases, and teardown of subscription and address space objects.

findings.text: Fault address lookup acquires the address space guard with a helper sensitive to execution context, locates the area for the address, returns it guarded when its beginning is at or before the address, otherwise attempts downward stack growth when permitted and returns the grown area after reducing exclusive ownership to shared, releasing the guard and reporting absence on any failure.

When growth may be needed the first variant prefers an atomic promotion of the guard; if promotion fails it releases and reacquires through the context sensitive helper, repeats the lookup and permission checks, invokes growth, then either demotes to shared on success or releases exclusive ownership on failure.
A second variant of the same lookup unconditionally takes shared ownership, queries for the covering area, keeps the guard only when an area is found and otherwise releases before reporting absence.
Without memory management unit support stack growth is never possible and the corresponding helper always signals shortage.
The batch free limit is 512 folios.
Removal of one page of a given size is delegated to the folio batching helper for a single unit marked as not compound.
Interprocessor synchronization target performs no action, table reclamation through RCU extracts the enclosing batch and frees it, and explicit synchronization waits for a grace period.

One build defers single table freeing through RCU with a callback that unwraps the descriptor then frees, while another build synchronizes immediately then frees directly; a small wrapper selects the active variant.

Table freeing accumulates pointers in a per gather batch allocated on demand from a single page; allocation failure forces invalidation plus immediate freeing, successful queueing flushes when the batch capacity is reached.

Subscription state for an address space holds a notification list, a flag recording interval tree use, a spin guard, a sequence counter plus a count of active invalidations, a cached interval tree root, a wait queue, and a deferred update list.
A lock validation object is published under a name indicating the start of notifier range invalidation for ordering checks.
Whether interval invalidation is in progress is determined by the parity of the sequence counter and the caller must already hold the subscription spin guard.

Starting interval invalidation takes the spin guard, raises the active count, scans for overlap with the requested span, marks the sequence odd when overlap exists, records the sequence for the caller, then releases the guard and returns the first overlapping subscriber if any.
Advancement to the next overlapping interval subscriber queries the tree for the successor within the adjusted span and unwraps the enclosing notifier, yielding absence when no successor exists.

Ending interval invalidation takes the spin guard and lowers the active count, returning early unless this is the last active range while odd; otherwise it advances the sequence to even, applies queued tree insertions and removals, clears the deferred list, releases the guard and wakes all waiters.

Release of interval subscribers walks the whole address span as a blockable release event, invoking a two phase start when available and queueing followups for a later finish pass or invoking a single phase callback otherwise, verifying success, then running queued finishes and closing the invalidation.

Release of classic subscribers iterates under sleepable RCU read protection invoking release callbacks, then detaches every remaining list entry under the spin guard, waits for readers, and the top level release dispatches to interval handling when enabled and to list handling when nonempty.

Three queries aggregate accessed state across classic subscribers under sleepable RCU protection: two OR together results from clear variants over a span and return the aggregate, while the single address test stops at the first positive.

Interval range invalidation iterates overlapping subscribers with the start sequence, preferring two phase start with queued finish and falling back to single phase, collects finishes, treats refusal as retryable only in nonblocking context and otherwise warns, closes the range on failure without requiring an outer end, and returns success or retry indication.

Classic range start invokes each interested subscriber under sleepable RCU protection with nonblocking markers when required, logs and warns on failure expecting retry indication in nonblocking context and forbidding an end callback on the failing party, and on any failure invokes end callbacks on parties that provide them before returning the failure.
Top level range start prefers interval handling when enabled and aborts on its error, otherwise delegates to classic list handling when nonempty and reports success when no subscriber exists.

Range end for classic subscribers iterates under sleepable RCU protection with nonblocking markers when required, while the top level end acquires a validation map, closes interval state when enabled, runs classic ends when nonempty, then releases the validation map.
Secondary translation cache invalidation for a span iterates classic subscribers under sleepable RCU protection and invokes the architecture specific callback where present.

Registration requires exclusive address space ownership and a live user count, lazily allocates and initializes subscription state with list, guard, sequence initialized to two, empty tree, wait queue and deferred list, takes all address space locks, publishes the state with release ordering, then either pins the address space and links the new classic subscriber under the spin guard or enables interval mode, finally dropping all locks.
A subscriber must not request both secondary cache invalidation and range start or end callbacks; such a combination is rejected as invalid.

Acquiring all locks requires exclusive address space ownership, takes a global mutex, marks every area for write, then in separate passes locks huge page mappings, other file mappings, and anon hierarchies, aborting with a full release if a signal is pending.

Per object locking is idempotent within one acquisition: anon hierarchies are locked once at the root with nesting under the address space guard tracked by a bit in the root, and file mappings are locked once on their mapping guard with nesting tracked by a dedicated flag using atomic update.

Releasing all locks requires exclusive ownership and that the global mutex is held, unlocks every anon hierarchy and file mapping encountered by iterating all areas, then releases the global mutex without undoing the write marks which persist until unlock or demotion.
